title: Gradual traffic pacing and beta expansion preflight
summary: Preflight for staged beta expansion: agree pacing windows, define canary metrics, finalize runbook owners, and list required test artifacts. Decided on 3 phased ramp with adaptive pacing, clarified alerting thresholds, and owners for fallback steps.
next_steps: Evan to publish final rollout runbook and share link by 2026-07-17
Priya to post updated alert thresholds to the ops channel and validate on staging by 2026-07-16
Zoe to run golden path regression suite focused on cache-warm scenarios by 2026-07-18
Liam to add KV pre-warm job to the scheduler and run a dry-run on staging by 2026-07-16
Maya to send stakeholder announcement draft to Comms and Legal by 2026-07-17
action_items: Priya: validate alerting thresholds and paging test (due 2026-07-16)
Liam: implement KV pre-warm job & dry-run (due 2026-07-16)
Zoe: execute targeted QA scenarios for batching/cache (due 2026-07-18)
Maya: draft external beta comms and get legal signoff (due 2026-07-17)
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-07-15 09:30 UTC — Duration: ~78 minutes; Attendees: Maya, Liam, Priya, Carlos, Evan, Zoe, Jonah

[00:00] Maya Chen: Okay let's kick off, thanks everyone for joining. This is our preflight for the beta expansion, we have 60ish minutes to lock pacing and the runbook and then any open Qs.
[00:18] Carlos Alvarez: Quick context — product signed off on the three-phase ramp; marketing timelines are fixed so we need to be confident on gradual traffic pacing. Main ask: no outages, predictable cost delta.
[00:34] Liam O'Connor: Right. Engineering's proposal was a three-stage increase: phase one 5% of peak for 24 hours, phase two 25% for 48 hours, phase three 100% but with throttled bursts. Each phase has canaries and automatic hold if SLOs cross thresholds.
[00:51] Priya Nair: Quick reminder — our SLOs are latency p50 < 80ms, p95 < 300ms, error rate < 0.5% for gen endpoints. Also cost guardrails: we want alerts at a 20% spend delta versus projected.
[01:08] Evan Brooks: I'll own the runbook publish and the final checklist. We should be explicit: who flips traffic, who watches which dashboard, and exact rollback criteria.
[01:25] Zoe Patel: From QA: we need a focused test on KV warmup — earlier dry runs had cold starts that spiked p95 for a few minutes. We need to validate the pre-warm job and warm cache hit rate before phase two.
[01:42] Jonah Reed: The scheduler pre-warm job is ready, it's just not enabled on staging. There's also the issue where K V cache eviction was too aggressive under a mixed workload, we've got a tuning PR but it needs one more validation.
[02:00] Maya Chen: Cool — let's step through the concrete checklist. Phase 0 — staging signoff: items are runbook completed, alert thresholds set, KV pre-warm dry-run succeeded, QA test pass, and golden path latency smoke. Who's comfortable checking off each?
[02:18] Priya Nair: Ops will own thresholds and the paging test. I can do a simulated error spike and ensure on-call pages within the target window.
[02:26] Liam O'Connor: Engineering will own the pre-warm job, dry-run, and the batching configuration checks. Also, note that batching knobs need to be conservative for phase one to keep latency predictable.
[02:45] Carlos Alvarez: Are we tracking cost impact in real time? We need a token-level projection in the dashboard and an auto-stop if spend delta > 35% before alerts.
[02:58] Evan Brooks: We have a cost projection widget but not an auto-stop. I don't love auto-stop for the whole rollout, we can set an aggressive alert and a manual hold by release manager.
[03:12] Maya Chen: Fine — manual hold for now, we can revisit auto-stop on subsequent rollouts.
[03:20] Zoe Patel: On QA, we noticed a transcription-ish artifact in logs — the KV cache key normalization was inconsistent so hits were lower. That was why K-V cash looked warm but was effectively cold. It's a naming mismatch in the pre-processor.
[03:41] Liam O'Connor: Yeah that was my bug — I changed a normalizer regex last sprint, missed a corner. PR open, will merge after dry-run passes.
[03:51] [04:00] Priya Nair: Timestamps are getting weird in the staging traces too — sometimes spans are missing when we have hop-by-hop sampling. We should ensure full tracing for canary traffic.
[04:12] Jonah Reed: We can enable 100% sampling for canary traffic to the tracing backend; it's cheap for the canary volume and helps root cause.
[04:25] Maya Chen: Ok. Next: metrics and rollback criteria. Let's be explicit here — if p95 increases > 50% above baseline for more than 10 minutes, immediate rollback. If error rate > 1% for 5 minutes, immediate hold and investigation. Any objections?
[04:46] Priya Nair: That seems reasonable. For cost, alert at 20% delta and release manager decides to hold at 35%.
[04:58] Evan Brooks: I'll add those numbers to the runbook. We also need a latency-correlated error classifier so we don't rollback for a single noisy keyspace.
[05:10] Zoe Patel: For that, QA will provide a list of high-variance prompts/keys to ignore for signal noise. We'll publish those in the ops doc.
[05:23] Carlos Alvarez: Speaking of keys, are we confident on multi-tenant isolation for the dedicated lanes? We planned to route beta traffic to a dedicated pool but with fallback to hosted. Could that cause noisy neighbors?
[05:40] Liam O'Connor: The dedicated pool is isolated at the allocation level; we do share some microservices like the routing layer. If the routing layer gets overloaded we have fallback to the hosted model pool with rate limiting.
[05:55] Priya Nair: Fallback routing needs to be seamless — we should pre-warm fallback caches too or we'll shift the problem. Maybe keep a small replica of KV in the fallback lane with a lower freshness requirement.
[06:12] Jonah Reed: We can create a lightweight replicate of hot keys to the fallback pool; it's an extra write but it's cheap relative to the risk.
[06:24] Maya Chen: Good. Let's capture that as an action — create a fallback KV replicate and test it.
[06:31] [06:45] Evan Brooks: On observability, dashboards: we need a single view that shows canary traffic %, latency breakdown by model variant, cache hit rate, infra CPU/GPU utilization, and cost delta. I'm thinking a single release dashboard with direct links to runbook anchors.
[06:59] Priya Nair: Also add the paging list and on-call copy so cross-team can notify the right people.
[07:07] Carlos Alvarez: We should include a business KPI view too — error impact to conversions. Product needs a quick yes/no on whether to proceed.
[07:17] Liam O'Connor: That means we need a short lagged metric capture — not more than 15 minutes. We can pipe a small event stream to the business dashboard.
[07:26] Zoe Patel: Back to QA — the golden path tests we ran last week passed but had a few p95 spikes under load. Those were correlated to cold KV misses and one model quantization fallback. We're going to retest with the KV pre-warm and the quant fallback disabled.
[07:46] Maya Chen: Good. Any security or compliance checklist items? This is internal but we need SOC2 audit readiness for the customer pilot.
[07:56] Carlos Alvarez: Legal wants the data retention policy called out, and SSO links for pilot partners. But that's a separate checklist; confirm that the pilot will use ephemeral identities and not export PII.
[08:10] Priya Nair: We'll enforce session masking on the pilot and ensure logs obfuscate any user identifiers. I will add the retention policy link to the runbook.
[08:20] [08:35] Evan Brooks: Ok let's walk through the proposed timeline: Friday 7/17 — staging signoff. Monday 7/20 — phase one at 5% for 24 hours. Wednesday 7/22 — phase two 25% for 48 hours. Start phase three on Friday 7/24 with controlled burst windows. Any blockers?
[08:58] Liam O'Connor: One blocker is the KV pre-warm dry-run which depends on a tuning PR — I need until EOD 7/16 to merge and run.
[09:07] Zoe Patel: QA needs access to a staging snapshot that mirrors the production hot key distribution; ops to provide that by 7/16.
[09:16] Priya Nair: I'll provision the snapshot and share details.
[09:21] Jonah Reed: Also, the scheduler's backfill for the pre-warm job has an edge-case race where a node restart cancels the backfill; I'll add a retry loop but need to validate. That's on me, due 7/16.
[09:34] [09:45] Maya Chen: Great — looks like owners are clear. Let's talk about communications: stakeholder cadence during rollout — who posts updates and cadence?
[09:55] Carlos Alvarez: Daily morning update for the first three days of a phase and midpoint check for longer phases. Release manager posts morning summary, product posts decision after each phase.
[10:07] Evan Brooks: I'll post morning summaries and link the dashboard. Also will call an all-hands if any critical thresholds breach.
[10:16] Zoe Patel: We should also automate a short post-phase report with key metrics so we keep an audit trail. QA can produce that template.
[10:25] Liam O'Connor: Technical deep-dive if we see steady p95 drift — we should have a plan for kernel fallback and model quantization off-ramp. But that's an escalation path, not first-line.
[10:40] Priya Nair: Agreed — escalation path: hold -> triage -> canary rollback -> failover to fallback pool -> rollback globally. Document each step in runbook with owner and timeline.
[10:53] Maya Chen: Any last concerns?
[10:58] Jonah Reed: One minor one — the routing rules for multi-region traffic. If we ramp in one region, we should keep other regions at baseline to reduce global blast radius.
[11:09] Carlos Alvarez: Good call — phase scoping should be regional by default, unless product asks for global. Keep it regional.
[11:17] Maya Chen: Okay final recap: Evan runbook (due 7/17), Priya alerts/paging (7/16), Liam KV pre-warm & merge (7/16), Zoe QA tests (7/18), Jonah scheduler retry fix (7/16), Maya outbound comms draft (7/17). We'll reconvene after staging signoff or earlier if a blocker pops up.
[11:40] Evan Brooks: I'll share the runbook link in the channel and tag owners.
[11:48] Zoe Patel: I'll upload QA artifacts and a post-phase report template.
[11:54] Priya Nair: I'll run a paging test tomorrow morning to verify alerting.
[12:01] Liam O'Connor: And I'll kick the dry-run tonight in staging and post results.
[12:12] Maya Chen: Thanks everyone. Meeting adjourned.

Optional notes: shared artifacts mentioned — rollout runbook (link to be posted), QA artifact bundle (to be uploaded), staging snapshot request. Some transcription artefacts noted: 'K V cash' mis-transcribed, occasional missing punctuation.

End of transcript.
